source.title: From Colors to Classes: Emergence of Concepts in Vision Transformers
source.authors: Teresa Dorszewski; Lenka Tetková; Robert Jenssen; Lars Kai Hansen; Kristoffer Wickstrøm

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures neuron labels and concept categories in vision transformers, but does not test whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs or whether neurons are polysemantic. Its label-based results are related to neuron interpretation but do not measure the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study assigns one CLIP-Dissect label per neuron and reports label counts and concept-category trends. It does not test multiple unrelated inputs for the same neuron, and mean-thresholding excludes lower-scoring neurons from the analysis. Results from cited prior work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study labels ViT and ResNet50 neurons with CLIP-Dissect and reports label counts and concept-category trends by layer and fine-tuning. It never measures whether single neurons respond to unrelated inputs. It mentions polysemanticity only in its limitations, citing Zoom In, and excludes low-scoring (possibly polysemantic) neurons by design. So it neither tests nor relies on the claim as a measured result.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors also stress that ViTs, despite global attention, build up concepts hierarchically like CNNs. They add that pretraining strategy affects concept categories.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses CLIP-Dissect to assign neuron labels and applies a per-layer mean similarity threshold; it does not reproduce or directly test a polysemanticity measurement from the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that a fixed threshold would give DINOv2 more labeled concepts, but state that category and fine-tuning analyses remain unchanged. They also report differences across models and fine-tuning tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise growth in unique neuron-label counts and a color-to-object category shift in ViTs, similar to ResNet50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ViT neuron labels progress from colors and textures in early layers to objects and organisms late, as in CNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning on CUB or bloodMNIST reduces the number of unique labels and shifts categories toward the task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning narrows and redirects the concepts assigned to ViT neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: DINOv2 has higher CLIP-Dissect similarity scores. The authors speculate this means more mono-semantic neurons, but do not test it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-distilled ViTs (DINOv2) may have more monosemantic neurons than other pretraining strategies.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted at The 3rd World Conference on eXplainable Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The study explicitly limits analysis to neurons whose labels exceed a per-layer mean similarity threshold, so lower-scoring or uninterpretable neurons are excluded. It assigns labels using one concept description per neuron and does not test whether individual neurons respond to several unrelated inputs. The word categories were produced with language models plus manual supervision and are acknowledged as subjective. Several layer-wise results are presented in figures without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted that directly test a claim version. Exact per-layer figure values and the ResNet50 comparison were not extracted because they concern label counts or category trends rather than polysemanticity.

untested.parts: Whether individual vision-model neurons respond to several unrelated inputs; not measured.
Superposition as a cause is mentioned only via citation; not tested.
Initialization, regularization or noise as causes; not tested.
Architectures and pretraining are compared on label categories, not on the share of polysemantic neurons.
No re-examination of canonical polysemantic neurons.
Threshold choice is discussed for label counts, not for polysemanticity judgments.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Zoom In (ref 21), noting that many neurons are not monosemantic, only to justify excluding non-interpretable neurons. The DINOv2 'more mono-semantic' remark is interpretive speculation from similarity scores, not a measured polysemanticity rate. ResNet50 label counts (Table 1) are also selection values.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether individual image-classifier neurons respond strongly to several unrelated inputs.
No language models or token/context polysemanticity are studied.
Does not test superposition or whether feature capacity pressure causes polysemanticity.
Does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity.
Compares architectures and pretraining/fine-tuning settings for concept labels, but does not measure how these change the share of polysemantic neurons or the performance cost of reducing that share.
Does not revisit canonical polysemantic neurons or test whether their apparently mixed inputs share a feature.
Uses an adaptive similarity-score threshold, but does not test how choices of activation range or explanation scoring change polysemanticity judgments.

rows.subject: all four ViTs (aggregate trend as described by the authors)
rows.size_stated: 12 transformer blocks; 768 neurons in each block's final MLP layer
rows.operation_detail: Count unique neuron labels by layer and categorize labeled neurons

conditions.value: early, middle, and late transformer blocks
ImageNet validation set and Broden; 113305 images total
mean similarity score within each layer

rows.measure: unique concepts per layer and distribution of labeled neurons across concept categories
rows.value: Early layers encode fewer than 100 different concepts; the number rises to around double that in late layers. Colors are prominent early and almost disappear in the last layer; objects and natural elements become dominant late. Textures and materials are mainly present in early and middle layers.
rows.note: The authors describe this as a shared trend across the ViTs. These category and layer trends do not measure mixed unrelated responses within a neuron.

rows.subject: three ViTs (average over models, as described by the authors)
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune pretrained models on CUB or bloodMNIST and reanalyze neuron labels
rows.measure: number and categories of unique neuron labels
rows.value: The number of encoded concepts decreases; colors increase, natural elements and organisms increase only slightly overall, and other categories decrease in proportion. The authors note a large late-layer increase in natural elements and organisms for CLIP, while DINOv2 and sup-ViT are almost unchanged.
rows.note: These are changes in assigned labels, not measurements of polysemantic-neuron prevalence.

rows.subject: three ViTs (average over models, as described by the authors)
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune pretrained models on CUB or bloodMNIST and reanalyze neuron labels
rows.measure: number and categories of unique neuron labels
rows.value: The number of encoded concepts decreases; colors and textures and patterns increase, while natural elements and organisms, objects and machines, and activities decrease.
rows.note: These are changes in assigned labels, not measurements of polysemantic-neuron prevalence.
